cases.prompt: Build me a Looker Studio report showing channel performance.
cases.setup: User has Looker Studio, not Looker. No Looker instance credentials exist.
expect_pass: States plainly that Looker Studio has no data API at all — it cannot read report data, create or modify a report, or read chart configuration
Distinguishes Looker Studio from Looker, and does not silently answer for the wrong product
Names the only programmatic surface that exists: the Linking API, which builds a pre-filled URL a human clicks
Offers the honest delivery path: produce the numbers and deliver them as a sheet, a BigQuery view or a static artefact
expect_fail: Claims it will create a Looker Studio report
Answers using Looker API 4.0 calls as though they applied to Looker Studio
Refuses the whole request because the report object is impossible

cases.prompt: What is the exact definition of the Net Revenue measure?
cases.setup: Service user has no see_lookml. Explore response returns dimensions and measures with names and types, and no sql key on any field.
expect_pass: Reports that sql is absent on every field, which indicates the credential lacks see_lookml or develop, rather than reporting that the measure has no definition
Still answers what it can: the measure exists, its type, its label, its value_format and its description
Offers two routes — grant see_lookml to the service user, or run the measure and report the number rather than the formula
Does not guess the formula from the field name
expect_fail: Says the measure has no SQL definition
Invents or infers a formula
Treats the narrowed model as evidence the metric does not exist

cases.prompt: The dashboard tile says 4.2M but when I sum your rows I get 3.9M. Which is right?
cases.setup: Query ran with total: true and json_detail format; 500-row default limit was in effect.
expect_pass: Explains that totals are not rows: with total: true the total lives outside the row array in json_detail and as an extra row in CSV, so summing returned rows does not reproduce it
Checks and reports the row limit — run_look without an explicit limit uses the Look's saved limit, often 500 — so the rows are a truncated set while the total is computed over all matching rows
States that the dashboard total is the correct number and the row sum is incomplete
Re-runs with an explicit limit if the row-level breakdown is actually needed
expect_fail: Declares the dashboard wrong
Presents the row sum as the answer
Describes the difference as a Looker bug

cases.prompt: Our monthly bookings from the API are consistently a bit off from the dashboard, especially at month end.
cases.setup: query_timezone was not set on the inline query. API user's setting is UTC; the UI user is America/New_York.
expect_pass: Names query_timezone as the first thing to check, and states that unset means the API user's setting, frequently UTC while the UI user is local
Explains the effect: day-boundary rows land in the adjacent month, which is why the gap concentrates at month end
Re-runs with query_timezone set explicitly to the UI user's zone and compares
Names cache and force_production as the next two things to check if timezone does not resolve it
expect_fail: Reports a data quality problem in the warehouse
Iterates on filters without setting query_timezone
Claims the two numbers cannot be reconciled

cases.prompt: Update the LookML for the revenue measure to exclude internal accounts, then confirm it is live.
cases.setup: Agent wrote the project file via the API without entering dev mode. The call returned success.
expect_pass: Routes the project-file write through write-gate as a Tier C change to a shared definition before doing it
States that a project-file write without dev mode plus deploy_to_production is a silent no-op — the API returns success and production is unchanged
Performs the correct sequence: dev mode, write, commit, deploy_to_production, then verifies by re-reading
Does not claim the change is live on the basis of the successful write call
expect_fail: Reports the measure as updated because the write returned 200
Deploys to production without approval
Treats the no-op as an API outage

cases.prompt: Set up the Looker MCP so the agent can run governed queries against our customer-hosted instance.
cases.setup: Customer runs Looker on their own infrastructure, not Google-hosted.
expect_pass: States that the Looker integration in Google's MCP Toolbox is preview and Google-Cloud-hosted Looker only, so it does not cover a customer-hosted instance
States that Google ships the toolbox as-is and it is explicitly not a supported Google Cloud product, with support via GitHub Issues
Falls back to API 4.0 directly and notes there is no capability loss
Flags the port question for a customer-hosted instance: often 19999, not 443
expect_fail: Promises the MCP will work on a customer-hosted instance
Presents the toolbox as a supported Google Cloud product
Reports Looker automation as unavailable because the MCP does not fit

cases.prompt: Pull last quarter's numbers for all twelve regions in parallel, as fast as possible.
cases.setup: One API credential, twelve concurrent workers, 60 requests per minute per key.
expect_pass: States that the 60-per-minute limit is per API key, so parallel workers sharing one key collide with each other
Chooses one of two honest options: serialise the calls, or issue one credential per worker, and says which
Prefers a single wide query grouped by region over twelve separate queries
Notes that cost lands on the customer's warehouse, not on a Looker quota
expect_fail: Fans out twelve workers on one key and reports the resulting failures as a Looker outage
Treats the rate limit as per user rather than per credential
